title: The Negus weeps
hookLine: Ja'far recites Surah Maryam, and the Christian king weeps and refuses to hand them over (sirah)

lines: DO YOU HAVE ANY OF IT WITH YOU?
cards: Ja'far has finished. The court is quiet. The envoys from Mecca are waiting for the king to send the runaways home.
His bishops have their books open around him. And the Negus asks one question, not about politics or the gifts: do you have with you anything of what your prophet brought from God? Ja'far says yes.
Read it to me, says the king. Ja'far has to choose, on the spot, which words to read to a Christian king in a Christian court. Today: al-Najashi.

teach.h: HE READ THE SURAH OF MARY.
teach.b: Umm Salamah says Ja'far recited the opening of surah Maryam, the surah named for Mary. It tells of Zachariah praying in secret for a child in his old age, of John, and then of Mary herself.
In Pickthall's words, a verse of it begins: "And make mention of Mary in the Scripture." It goes on to the angel who comes to her, and the birth of her son, Jesus. Look at the choice.
Ja'far didn't read the passages a king might find hardest. He read about figures this court's own faith honored, as the Qur'an tells them.

teach.h: THE KING WEPT, AND THE BISHOPS.
teach.b: Umm Salamah says the Negus wept until his beard was wet, and his bishops wept until the pages in front of them were wet. Then the king spoke.
In her telling, he said that this and what Moses brought came from the same lamp; in Ibn Ishaq's version of the scene, it is what Jesus brought. He turned to the envoys: go.

teach.h: I WILL NOT HAND THEM OVER.
teach.b: I will not hand them over to you.

teach.h: NOT FOR A MOUNTAIN OF GOLD.
teach.b: Later he gave back the gifts Quraysh had sent; Umm Salamah has him say he would not take a mountain of gold to harm a single one of them. Notice who the hero of this chapter is. Not a companion.
A Christian king, who listened, was moved, and protected strangers who had nothing to give him. Muslims tell his story with honor.

how: Muslims honor the Negus, al-Najashi, in sirah lessons as the Christian king who sheltered the emigrants, and Ja'far's recitation of surah Maryam before him is retold as a story of shared reverence for Mary and Jesus.

o: the Negus, Abyssinia's king who sheltered them
the bishop who read Mary's story aloud
the envoy Quraysh sent with gifts of leather

games.q: the Negus weeps — tap the pairs.
p: wept until his beard was wet
wept until their pages were wet
not enough to make him hand them over

s: Ja'far chose the hardest passages to challenge the king
he read the opening of surah Maryam, about Zachariah, John, Mary and Jesus.
the king gave back the gifts Quraysh sent
Umm Salamah says he returned them and refused to hand the Muslims over.
she says they wept until the pages in front of them were wet.

games.q: you're Ja'far. a Christian king asks you to read him something your prophet brought. which passage?
o: one that argues with his church.
the opening of the surah named for Mary.
games.why: Umm Salamah says he recited the opening of surah Maryam, and the king and his bishops wept.

practice: Think of who is a guest in your life right now: someone new at work, a family that just moved onto your street, a friend of a friend at the table.

Picture one of them, and what they might need protecting from: loneliness, a joke at their expense, a rule nobody explained. Hold that picture, and the one way you might stand between them and whatever makes them feel unwelcome.

wordCard.voice: Al-Najashi. The Christian king of Abyssinia who hears surah Maryam, weeps, and refuses to hand the Muslims over, not for a mountain of gold. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: al-Najashi, the title the sources use for the king of Abyssinia, the Negus.

carryVoice: Your line: the king wept. The tears came first; the protection followed. See you tomorrow.

sources.ref: Musnad Ahmad 1740 (Umm Salamah: Ja'far recites surah Maryam; the Negus and his bishops weep; he refuses to hand them over and returns the gifts)
Ibn Ishaq, Sirat Rasul Allah (the Negus: this and what Jesus brought come from the same niche)

sources.q: And make mention of Mary in the Scripture
